speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the root cause, please tell me: are you experiencing recurrent fractures from minor trauma, and do you have a family history of similar bone issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly, labial fusion), virilization (hirsutism, severe acne), delayed menarche, and a history of fractures suggests a classic form of CAH, potentially complicated by osteoporosis due to chronic cortisol/catecholamine issues or treatment side effects. I need to confirm the specific enzyme deficiency and assess bone density.

REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone level, Serum Cortisol, ACTH stimulation test, DEXA scan of the lumbar spine.
